lessons.title: Recognize hazards and prepare for emergencies
lessons.reading: きけんをみつけ、きんきゅうじにそなえる

objectives.text: Match hazards in the building with the preparations they require
Check escape equipment and contact arrangements in your work area
Keep a safe distance and report suspicious objects

sections.title: Think about risks in specific situations
sections.body: Accommodation facilities bring together people of different ages and levels of familiarity with the building for extended stays. Fire, earthquakes and sudden illness can occur even during busy service periods. Rather than waiting for an accident, imagine what could happen in your own work area. For example, decide in advance whom to contact and which way to guide guests if you discover smoke in a corridor at night. Preparation means considering not only the hazard but also who could be affected and what to do first. Keep combustible linen and paper away from ignition sources, and dispose of cigarette ends according to facility procedures.

sections.title: Connect equipment, routes and procedures
sections.body: Training involves more than remembering where exits are. Check the actual route from your work area and practise how you would explain it. Learn from the responsible staff where alarms, extinguishers and guest-room evacuation equipment are located and how to use them correctly. Do not try unfamiliar equipment for the first time during an emergency. Read the facility procedures for sudden illness, accidents and fires, and identify both the assigned staff and their backups. Learn about infection risks, how infections spread and the facility response instead of relying on guesses.

sections.title: Notice unfamiliar objects and behavior
sections.body: During rounds, observe luggage, corridors and the surroundings. An object with no identifiable owner is not necessarily dangerous, but touching it carelessly to find out is also inappropriate. Report its location, discovery time, appearance and surroundings to the person in charge. Judge concerning behavior by observed actions and facility criteria, not a person’s nationality or appearance. Do not try to resolve a dangerous situation alone; request assistance through the facility procedure.

terms.meaning: The route used to reach a safe place
Equipment provided to help people evacuate
An object whose owner or circumstances are unclear and whose safety needs checking

example.situation: Before a night shift, you check a guest floor you have not worked on before.
steps: Walk to the emergency exits and check for obstructions.
Ask an experienced colleague where the alarms, extinguishers and procedures are.
Explain who contacts help and who guides guests in a medical emergency.

practice.prompt: Imagine your work floor. Make a table for fire, sudden illness and a suspicious object, identifying places to check, people to contact and actions to avoid.
expectedPoints: Name specific locations
Refer to facility procedures
Avoid approaching hazards alone

questions.prompt: What is the best preparation before working on an unfamiliar floor?
choices: Photograph an exit sign without checking the route
Learn how to use the extinguisher only when a fire occurs
Check routes, equipment and contact arrangements beforehand, and practise your role
Ignore training during busy periods
questions.explanation: Connecting locations, equipment use and responsibilities beforehand reduces uncertainty during an emergency.

questions.prompt: You discover a suspicious object with no known owner. What should you do?
choices: Open it alone to inspect the contents
Observe from a safe position and report it to the person in charge
Kick it aside in front of guests
Pretend not to have seen it
questions.explanation: Do not touch it carelessly. Describe its location and appearance and follow facility procedures.

questions.prompt: What is an appropriate way to prepare for infectious diseases?
choices: Memorize only the names of symptoms
Learn the risks, how infection spreads and the facility response, and check procedures
Use exactly the same response for every disease
Give guests a diagnosis based on your own guess
questions.explanation: Understand the risks and transmission and prepare to act according to the facility manual.

questions.prompt: Which action helps prevent fire?
choices: Keep combustible linen next to an ignition source
Mix cigarette ends with paper waste
Keep combustibles away from ignition sources and dispose of cigarette ends as instructed
Do not check storage locations until a fire starts
questions.explanation: Separating combustibles from ignition sources and disposing of cigarette ends properly reduces the risk of ignition.

questions.prompt: What is appropriate preparation before work regarding fire alarms, extinguishers and guest-room evacuation equipment?
choices: Remember only the locations and try using the equipment for the first time in an emergency
Assume that seeing photographs makes training and facility procedures unnecessary
Learn each location and correct use from the responsible staff, and confirm through the necessary training
Remember just one device on a floor outside your assigned area
questions.explanation: The source requires both the location and use of equipment. Reading alone does not establish operating skill; confirm the facility’s equipment and procedures with staff and through training.

illustration.caption: Decisions and actions for recognizing hazards and preparing for emergencies
illustration.alt: Diagram linking the hazards to check with the corresponding preparations and responses

lessons.title: Safe actions during fires, earthquakes and medical emergencies
lessons.reading: かさい・じしん・きゅうびょうじのあんぜんこうどう

objectives.text: Distinguish the limits of initial firefighting from the need to evacuate
Explain guidance using emergency stairs
Organize the information to give when calling 119

sections.title: Protect yourself when discovering a fire
sections.body: Alert people nearby and follow facility procedures for calling for help and guiding evacuation. Attempt initial firefighting only when you have a safe escape route and can use a trained method safely. Strong smoke or heat, a threatened escape route or flames reaching the ceiling means it is not a situation in which to keep fighting the fire. Evacuate immediately in a safe direction. Do not memorize the textbook statement about switching to indoor firefighting equipment after flames reach the ceiling as a universal instruction for all staff. Fire and Disaster Management Agency guidance calls for prompt evacuation once fire reaches the ceiling.

sections.title: Check whether the evacuation route is safe
sections.body: During a fire, do not direct guests to elevators. Follow the evacuation plan and announcements and guide them to safe emergency stairs or other designated routes. Stay low when moving through smoke and try to avoid inhaling it. During an earthquake, do not give a blanket instruction to run without checking the surroundings while shaking continues. First protect yourself, then check the facility procedure and route conditions before moving. Stairs are not automatically safe: report smoke or damage and do not lead guests toward danger.

sections.title: Give 119 a specific location and situation
sections.body: Call 119 for fire or ambulance assistance. Provide the address as well as the facility name, the floor and exact location, whether it is a fire or medical emergency, and what you can observe. Do not invent answers when unsure; follow the dispatcher’s questions. Share information within the facility and arrange for someone to guide responders from the entrance. Do not independently diagnose a guest or decide treatment: follow emergency procedures and dispatcher instructions. Record who reported, when and to whom the situation was handed over so repeated checks do not obstruct the response.

sections.title: Describe the person’s condition in a medical emergency call
sections.body:
After explaining the location in a medical emergency call, describe who is affected, since when, and their condition as far as you know. The dispatcher may ask about symptoms, age and sex. Do not confuse an age confirmed with the person or companion with a guess from appearance. Say “I do not know” when necessary and follow the questions. If asked about consciousness or breathing, report the observed condition rather than deciding a diagnosis yourself. Also provide the caller’s name and a telephone number where they can still be reached. For example, in a fictional exercise, practice separating location, circumstances and the basis of information: “A guest suddenly became unwell in the dining venue on the second floor. Their companion says they are sixty-five. I will describe the symptoms I can currently confirm.” Do not practice waiting until every detail has been gathered before calling. Listen to the dispatcher and ask nearby staff to take roles such as meeting responders at the entrance.

The Type 2 source also recommends encouraging a suddenly unwell guest to seek medical attention as far as possible. Follow the facility procedure, coordinate with the responsible person and help with consultation or finding a medical institution. However, in a highly urgent situation such as sudden breathing abnormalities, do not wait to call 119 until referrals or the full interview are finished. Staff must not diagnose or declare the condition mild and obstruct medical attention or an emergency call. Report what is confirmed and follow dispatcher instructions.

terms.meaning: Firefighting during an early stage, while ensuring safety
A route for withdrawing from danger
Guiding people toward a safe location

example.situation: You see fire and smoke at the back of the breakfast area.
steps: Alert nearby people and the person in charge, and assign calling and guidance roles.
Check your escape route and keep initial actions within safe limits.
Evacuate rather than continue firefighting if flames or smoke spread.
Do not direct guests toward an elevator.

practice.prompt: Practise aloud what you would tell 119 about a medical emergency in the facility. Also explain what changes if flames reach the ceiling. Then assign the roles of emergency responder, caller and entrance guide, and separately convey the address, location inside the facility, confirmed symptoms, age and similar details, and the caller’s contact information. Answer questions about unknown details without guessing.
expectedPoints: Identify both the address and the internal location
Describe observed facts
Choose evacuation over continuing to fight the fire
Report symptoms, age and similar details as far as they have been confirmed
Do not invent unknown details; follow the dispatcher’s questions and instructions

questions.prompt: While using an extinguisher, you see flames reach the ceiling. What is the best action?
choices: Find indoor firefighting equipment and always continue
Ask guests to fight the fire
Take photographs before deciding
Stop firefighting and evacuate immediately
questions.explanation: An extinguisher is unlikely to control a fire that has reached the ceiling. Prioritize your own and guests’ evacuation.

questions.prompt: What should you say when calling 119?
choices: Give the address, location within the building, type of emergency and known circumstances
The hotel name makes the address unnecessary
Present a guessed cause as fact
Hang up without answering questions
questions.explanation: Give specific information so responders can identify the scene and situation, and answer the dispatcher’s questions.

questions.prompt: Which instruction is appropriate during a fire?
choices: Guide everyone to the nearest elevator
Check the plan and route conditions and guide guests to safe emergency stairs or another designated route
Send all guests back to their rooms to wait
Assume there is an exit in the direction of the smoke
questions.explanation: Avoid elevators and also check routes for smoke or damage.

questions.prompt: The 119 dispatcher asks an unwell guest’s age, which is not yet confirmed. What should you do?
choices: State a definite age from appearance
Say it is unknown, report confirmed symptoms and location, and follow the dispatcher’s questions
Hang up until the age is known
Substitute a guessed diagnosis for the age
questions.explanation: Do not turn guesses into facts. Give symptoms and age as far as known and do not delay urgent contact to gather information.

questions.prompt: After the location, which information should be added in response to the dispatcher?
choices: Only advertising copy for a stay package
Sales targets and staff seniority
Confirmed symptoms, age and similar details, plus the caller’s name and contact information
A guessed diagnosis and unrelated guests’ records
questions.explanation: Report the person’s condition and a reachable contact as far as known. Do not declare a diagnosis or provide unrelated personal information.

questions.prompt: How should medical referral and calling 119 be handled for a suddenly unwell guest?
choices: Wait to call 119 even in an emergency until referral is finished
Staff must diagnose before recommending care
Help with medical consultation, and in urgent cases call 119 without waiting for referrals or all details
Describe everyone as mildly ill without checking
questions.explanation: Encouraging medical attention is compatible with prompt emergency contact. Do not delay urgent calls; report confirmed conditions and follow dispatcher instructions.

questions.prompt: Which decision about initial firefighting follows the lesson?
choices: Fight a small-looking fire without checking an escape route
Attempt only within trained, safely manageable limits with an escape route; evacuate rather than continue if smoke, heat or escape-route danger develops
Once fire reaches the ceiling, all general staff must continue with indoor firefighting equipment
Delay calls and evacuation guidance until firefighting ends
questions.explanation: Judge initial firefighting and evacuation by safety conditions. Do not reinterpret the lesson as continued firefighting in danger; follow facility reporting and evacuation procedures.

illustration.caption: Decisions and actions during fire, earthquakes and medical emergencies
illustration.alt: Diagram showing safe escape routes, emergency stairs and the information needed for an emergency call

lessons.title: Protect guests through information security and considerate support
lessons.reading: じょうほうとはいりょでおきゃくさまをまもる

objectives.text: Choose actions that prevent personal-data leaks
Ask guests what assistance they need
Distinguish assistance dogs from pets

sections.title: Names and addresses are also part of safety management
sections.body: Protecting guests means preventing information leaks as well as injuries. When handling names, addresses and accommodation details, check whether other people can see the screen or paperwork or hear the conversation. Do not reveal a room number or confirm a stay merely because someone claims to know the guest: follow the facility’s verification procedure. Report misplaced documents or a misdirected message to the person in charge rather than conceal the error, and prevent further disclosure. Even for work purposes, do not use unapproved devices or take information home without authorization.

sections.title: Ask the guest what support they want
sections.body: Do not assume an older guest or a guest with a disability is unable to do something based on appearance. Offer assistance and ask the person what kind of support they want. Provide concrete information about steps and corridor conditions. Rather than moving the person or their mobility aid without asking, confirm their wishes and a safe method and coordinate with the responsible staff. When sharing information about possible evacuation support, also limit disclosure to those who need it.

sections.title: Receiving guests with assistance dogs
sections.body: Guide dogs, mobility assistance dogs and hearing dogs support people with disabilities and are not treated as ordinary pets. Hotels and inns generally accept them under Japan’s assistance-dog legislation. When verification is needed, check identification markings or certification politely. If arrangements are needed for other users, such as someone with allergies, do not impose an immediate blanket refusal; involve the person in charge to confirm the circumstances with the guest. Ordinary staff should not decide statutory exceptional circumstances solely from a facility rule banning pets.

terms.meaning: Information concerning an identifiable person
Information reaching someone who should not receive it
Guide dogs, mobility assistance dogs and hearing dogs

example.situation: A guest arrives with a guide dog at a hotel that does not allow pets.
steps: Do not refuse solely because of the ordinary pet rule.
Politely check assistance-dog identification or certification if needed.
Ask the guest what guidance or support they want.
Refer circumstances requiring adjustments to the person in charge.

practice.prompt: Explain your first checks when someone asks for another guest’s room number and when a wheelchair user asks about moving around the facility.
expectedPoints: Follow the personal-information verification procedure
Ask what assistance the person wants
Do not judge solely from appearance or an unverified claim

questions.prompt: Someone claiming to be a guest’s friend asks for the room number. What should you do?
choices: Give it because the person seems friendly
Follow verification procedures and do not disclose it on your own
Also give the guest’s address
Ask on social media
questions.explanation: Accommodation information requires protection. A visitor’s statement alone does not authorize disclosure.

questions.prompt: What is the first appropriate action toward a guest who may need assistance?
choices: Ask the person what support they want
Move their body without asking
Explain only to their companion and ignore the guest
Give everyone identical assistance
questions.explanation: People need different support. Confirm the guest’s wishes.

questions.prompt: Which response to a guest with an assistance dog is appropriate?
choices: Apply identical rules to every dog without distinction
Immediately refuse because pets are prohibited
Understand the acceptance principle and make necessary checks or arrangements
Always refuse because extra cleaning might be needed
questions.explanation: Do not confuse assistance dogs with pets. Make necessary checks and refer exceptional circumstances to the responsible person.

illustration.caption: Decisions and actions for protecting guest information and providing support
illustration.alt: Diagram connecting personal-information protection, asking about assistance and assistance-dog reception

lessons.title: Daily personal hygiene and a clean building
lessons.reading: まいにちのみだしなみとせいけつなかんない

objectives.text: Check appearance from both service and hygiene perspectives
Connect discovered dirt with cleaning and reporting
Watch temperature and humidity for mold and pest risks

sections.title: Check cleanliness before and during work
sections.body: A clean uniform at the start of the shift does not guarantee continued hygiene. Keep hair and nails tidy and check again if they become soiled during work. Secure long hair so it does not interfere with tasks or contaminate food. Avoid strong perfume during service because it may bother guests or interfere with food aromas. Distinguish facility rules on conspicuous appearance from hygiene-related reasons. Wear shoes correctly so you can move steadily. Posture and movements also help guests feel at ease.

sections.title: Wash hands when changing tasks
sections.body: Make handwashing a daily habit and wash before handling food or tableware. Wearing gloves does not remove the need to wash hands. Pay attention to task boundaries so you do not touch clean tableware or guest supplies immediately after handling dirty objects. The textbook also mentions gargling, but do not teach that gargling alone prevents infection or food poisoning. Combine health reporting, handwashing and cleaning according to their different purposes.

sections.title: Inspect both visible and hidden areas
sections.body: Check floors, walls, windows, tables, chairs and supplies, and clean dirt rather than leaving it. Keep back-of-house areas clean even though guests rarely see them. During wet-floor cleaning, also prevent slips by warning people about the area. When temperature or humidity changes, look for signs of mold or pests and report where they are found. Do not independently select chemicals outside your responsibility; follow cleaning and pest-control procedures and the responsible staff. Check not just that cleaning occurred, but also whether the problem remains.

terms.meaning: Managing cleanliness and work conditions to prevent harm to health
Keeping clothing, hair, nails, posture and other aspects suitable for work
Insects that harm hygiene or the facility environment

example.situation: While setting out tableware, you stop to pick up an object from the floor.
steps: Separate the dirty task from handling clean tableware.
Follow the facility procedure for handwashing and other necessary steps.
Check floor cleanliness and safety before returning to the tableware task.

practice.prompt: For uniform, hair, nails, hands, floors, furniture and back-of-house areas, list what to check before and during work.
expectedPoints: Explain hygiene reasons, not appearance alone
Include handwashing at task changes
Include areas hidden from guests

questions.prompt: What is appropriate before handling food?
choices: Apply a large amount of perfume
Assume gloves eliminate handwashing
Wash hands and start work in a clean condition
Skip checking a uniform because it is white
questions.explanation: Handwashing and a clean working condition are necessary before touching food or tableware.

questions.prompt: You find dirt in a storeroom that guests cannot see. What should you do?
choices: Leave it because it is hidden
Clean it according to procedures to maintain cleanliness
Hide it elsewhere
Cover it with fragrance
questions.explanation: Back-of-house areas are also subject to hygiene management.

questions.prompt: What is appropriate for long hair and uniforms when handling food?
choices: Tidy them only before work and ignore later soiling
Keep hair and nails tidy, maintain a clean uniform and respond to soiling during work
Hide uniform dirt with perfume
Hair on an unseen side may touch food
questions.explanation: Maintain cleanliness throughout the shift. Check hair-contamination prevention and uniform condition; scent does not hide dirt.

questions.prompt: The uniform is clean but there is strong perfume. What is appropriate?
choices: Expensive perfume is acceptable
It is always acceptable if the worker does not carry food
Separately from cleanliness, avoid strong fragrance because of its effect on service and dining
A clean uniform means scent needs no check
questions.explanation: Fragrance affects comfort and food aromas. Clothing cleanliness alone does not decide suitability.

questions.prompt: In humid weather, you find a mold-like mark on a wall. What should you do?
choices: Do not record it if guests cannot see it
Mix chemicals outside your responsibility
Treat weather as unrelated to hygiene
Report the location and condition and follow facility cleaning and pest-control procedures
questions.explanation: Look for mold and pest signs associated with temperature and humidity and report their locations. Do not independently choose or mix chemicals.

questions.prompt: What is appropriate when checking shoes and waiting posture?
choices: Step on shoe heels and move quickly
Wear shoes correctly, straighten your back and standing posture, and ensure stable movement
Shoes and movements are irrelevant if the uniform is clean
Block the corridor when guests are absent
questions.explanation: Grooming includes correct shoe wear, posture and movement. Check appearance and stable movement together.

questions.prompt: How should guidance on hair color and nail decoration be given?
choices: Explain hygiene reasons and facility appearance rules as identical
Always allow expensive decorations
Distinguish hygiene reasons from facility rules and confirm cleanliness suitable for the task
Hair may touch food if appearance is tidy
questions.explanation: Separate hygiene reasons such as cleanliness and contamination prevention from facility appearance standards.

questions.prompt: What is appropriate for a worker who habitually gargles?
choices: Use gargling alone and skip handwashing and cleaning
Gargling removes the need to report illness
No washing is needed before touching food
Combine washing, cleaning and health reporting according to their purposes rather than relying on gargling alone
questions.explanation: The source does not mean one habit is sufficient. Continue hygiene actions suited to each purpose.

illustration.caption: Decisions and actions for daily appearance and cleanliness
illustration.alt: Diagram showing personal-hygiene checks and cleaning areas visible and hidden from guests

lessons.title: Connect equipment defects with environmental improvements
lessons.reading: せつびのふびとかんきょうかいぜんをつなぐ

objectives.text: Report minor equipment abnormalities specifically
Record guests’ requests as improvement proposals
Reduce resource waste while maintaining safety and comfort

sections.title: Do not ignore small abnormalities
sections.body: A small defect in air conditioning, equipment, tools, furniture or interiors can lead to an accident if use continues. Do not decide alone that something is acceptable because it still works. Tell the facilities staff what is wrong, in which room, when and under what conditions. Follow facility procedures to keep guests away from a dangerous area. Do not carry out repairs beyond your qualifications or responsibilities, and clarify who will authorize use to resume after repairs.

sections.title: Record requests to improve usability
sections.body: When a guest asks about handrails or ramps, confirm and record the location and circumstances causing difficulty. Do not immediately promise installation; pass on information the responsible team can evaluate. Level 2 also introduces universal design: designing facilities and products to be usable by as many people as possible, regardless of age, sex or disability. In staff-only areas, organize documents and supplies and keep routes usable to protect workers as well.

sections.title: Build energy and resource savings into work
sections.body: Saving electricity and water does not mean switching off required safety equipment or abandoning cleaning. Review lighting and water use according to occupancy and operating procedures. Check content and quantity before printing to avoid unnecessary paper use. Separate waste according to facility and local categories so recyclable materials are not mixed with other waste. An improvement proposal should explain both what can be reduced and how safety, hygiene and guest comfort will be protected. Practical action means noticing daily waste, not merely remembering the term SDGs.

terms.meaning: A condition that does not meet what is needed
Organizing necessary items so they are easy and safe to use
Reducing unnecessary energy consumption

example.situation: A guest says a corridor handrail is loose and asks for another handrail elsewhere.
steps: Record the dangerous defect separately from the future improvement request.
Promptly report the defect’s location and condition to facilities staff.
Confirm the reason for the request and pass it on as an improvement proposal.

practice.prompt: Write one defect report and one resource-saving proposal. Include the location, conditions, recipient and safety considerations.
expectedPoints: Describe the abnormality specifically
Do not perform repairs beyond your responsibility
Do not sacrifice safety or hygiene

questions.prompt: A guest-room light is making an unusual noise. What should you do?
choices: Do not report it because it still works
Ask the guest to dismantle it
Report the location and condition and follow procedures about its use
Repair the wiring without authorization
questions.explanation: Even minor defects can cause accidents. Report concrete details to the responsible staff.

questions.prompt: Which environmental action is appropriate?
choices: Turn off emergency equipment to save power
Review unnecessary printing and water use while maintaining safety and hygiene
Put all waste into the same bag
Skip cleaning
questions.explanation: Resource savings should maintain safety and hygiene.

questions.prompt: A guest says a handrail at a step would help. What should you do?
choices: Promise it will definitely be installed tomorrow
Start construction on your own
Confirm and record the location and difficulty and send an improvement proposal to the responsible staff
Do not record equipment-related requests
questions.explanation: Record the circumstances and specific location and refer the decision to the responsible staff.

questions.prompt: Boxes of documents are stacked in a storeroom passage. What should you do?
choices: Organize even areas guests do not enter so workers can pass safely
Leave them if guests cannot see them
Narrow the passage to increase storage
Block the exit without contacting the responsible staff
questions.explanation: Areas out of guests’ sight also require organized documents and supplies and safe circulation routes.

questions.prompt: What is appropriate when improving waste separation?
choices: Put everything in one bag to speed up collection
Check facility and local categories and keep recoverable materials separate
Waste separation is unnecessary if paper is not used
Turn off safety equipment to save energy
questions.explanation: Confirm waste categories using facility and local rules. Reducing waste does not mean omitting safety equipment or hygiene.

questions.prompt: What should you check when proposing water savings to your supervisor?
choices: Only consider water use and eliminate cleaning
Ignore guest preferences and hygiene
Explain the reduction and its effects on safety, hygiene and guest comfort
Stop all necessary washing water as well
questions.explanation: When proposing resource savings, check whether safety and hygiene can be maintained and whether guests’ use will be affected.

illustration.caption: Decisions and actions for equipment defects and improvements
illustration.alt: Diagram connecting defect discovery, reporting, improvement requests and resource-saving proposals

lessons.title: Understand lodging law and records accurately
lessons.reading: りょかんぎょうほうときろくをただしくりかいする

objectives.text: Explain the relationship between permission, facility standards and hygiene
Distinguish the three business categories without relying on price
Check current guest-register fields and the retention period

sections.title: Permission and facility standards
sections.body: The Hotel Business Act concerns proper operation of accommodation businesses and public health. Operating a lodging business generally requires permission from the prefectural governor or equivalent authority. In cities with public health centers and in special wards, the authority is the mayor or ward mayor. Distinguish the consultation office from the legal permission-granting authority. Check structural and equipment standards for room size, ventilation, natural light, toilets and washbasins. Operators and managers confirm applicable standards with the public health center or other authority according to business category, local ordinances and equipment conditions; frontline staff report abnormalities or changes.

sections.title: Use definitions to distinguish the three categories
sections.body: The Act distinguishes hotel/ryokan business, simple lodging business and boarding-house business. Simple lodging primarily provides structures and equipment for shared sleeping accommodation by many people; it does not simply mean inexpensive accommodation. Boarding-house business charges accommodation fees by units of at least one month. A single long-stay guest does not by itself determine the category. Check the permitted business category and statutory definition rather than deciding from the name or price.

sections.title: Check current register fields and retention
sections.body: Prepare accurate guest registers and store them appropriately. Under the implementing regulations checked on October 31, 2026, record names, addresses, contact details and other required information, and retain the register for three years from its creation. Additional nationality and passport-number fields apply to foreign guests who do not have an address in Japan. Check any additional local requirements. Do not teach the textbook’s occupation field as a current basic requirement under this Act. Standardize the collection purpose, required fields, storage location and authorized access within the facility, and prevent personal-data leaks.

sections.title: Use records to verify hygiene and safety measures
sections.body: Maintain cleaning, disinfection and pest control, and properly manage fire-safety equipment and escape routes. Safety measures may arise not only from lodging law but also fire-safety legislation and local ordinances. Following an inspection or direction from a public health center or local authority, organize the findings, responsible staff, deadlines and improvement results and confirm corrective action. Depending on the violation, suspension, cancellation of permission or penalties may apply. Do not conceal problems from the person in charge or guess penalty amounts when explaining them.

terms.meaning: Legislation concerning accommodation businesses and public health

terms.reading: かんいしゅくしょえいぎょう
terms.meaning: A business primarily providing structures and equipment for shared sleeping accommodation by many people

terms.reading: しゅくはくしゃめいぼ
terms.meaning: A register recording and retaining required guest information

example.situation: A new employee says registers require occupation and inexpensive accommodation is called simple lodging.
steps: Check current register fields and correct the distinction between occupation and contact details.
Confirm the business category by the statutory structure-and-equipment definition, not price.
Notify the staff responsible for updating explanations and forms.

practice.prompt: For permission, categories, registers and supervision, write one point requiring a current-system check rather than relying only on the textbook.
expectedPoints: Distinguish the consultation office from the permission authority
Simple lodging is not a low-price category
Contact details and three-year retention
Record directions and corrective results

questions.prompt: Which understanding of simple lodging is appropriate?
choices: The lowest-priced accommodation always qualifies
Focus on structures and equipment primarily for shared sleeping accommodation by many people
Any long-stay guest makes it qualify
The name hotel rules it out
questions.explanation: Check statutory definitions and permission, not just price or name.

questions.prompt: Which are current basic guest-register fields under lodging law?
choices: Name, address and occupation only
Name only
Name, address, contact details and other required information
The guest’s salary
questions.explanation: Contact details have replaced occupation as a basic field. Confirm the scope of additional foreign-guest information according to residence in Japan and other conditions.

questions.prompt: How should guest registers be retained?
choices: For three years from creation
Discard immediately after check-out
According to the staff member’s preference
Only until the next morning
questions.explanation: Follow the retention period in the implementing regulations while also protecting personal information.

questions.prompt: What should a manager do after public health center directions?
choices: No record is needed because the directions were oral
Keep it secret within one department
Wait until a problem occurs
Record findings, responsible staff, deadlines and improvement results, and confirm correction
questions.explanation: Record responsibility and results so improvements can be carried out and verified.

illustration.caption: Decisions and actions for lodging law and record management
illustration.alt: Diagram linking business permission, categories, guest registers, inspection and corrective action

lessons.title: Emergency management that protects staff
lessons.reading: じゅうぎょういんをまもるきんきゅうかんり

objectives.text: Explain training and equipment management based on the fire plan
Judge health reporting and work adjustments
Protect yourself when dealing with suspicious objects or vomit

sections.title: Train and keep equipment ready
sections.body: Managers should review not only attendance but also whether calling, firefighting and evacuation roles were carried out. For specified fire-prevention premises, applicable law may require extinguishing and evacuation drills at least twice yearly; confirm reporting-drill frequency in the fire plan. Check applicability with fire-safety personnel for the facility’s size and conditions and reflect it in the plan. Keep objects away from fire doors and evacuation routes, and maintain alarm equipment. Do not assume all buildings have identical equipment and inspection requirements. Keep combustible linen, paper waste and magazines away from ignition sources, and dispose of cigarette ends as instructed.

sections.title: Do not conceal symptoms based on your own judgment
sections.body: Report diarrhea, vomiting, fever, cough, sore throat or other symptoms before work and consult the responsible person about attendance and medical assessment. Report illness developing during a shift even when busy. Managers should check tasks, food contact and effects on colleagues and adjust work. Do not use the textbook’s 37.5°C figure as a universal boundary for every infection or work restriction. Symptoms still require reporting below that temperature, and return-to-work conditions must be checked against facility procedures and medical or public health instructions.

sections.title: Do not handle suspicious objects or vomit alone at risk
sections.body: When you notice a suspicious object or dangerous behavior, coordinate with the person in charge and other staff, involving police where necessary. Do not approach when your safety cannot be maintained. If vomit is found, keep people away and notify the responsible staff. Trained personnel should use gloves, a mask, gown and other required protection and avoid splashing. To prevent secondary infection such as norovirus, follow the current facility procedure and product instructions for gentle wiping, appropriate disinfection, rinsing with water, sealed disposal and handwashing afterward. Do not touch it barehanded or mix disinfectants on your own.

sections.title: Hand over information without unauthorized removal
sections.body: Do not copy a customer register onto a personal laptop and take it home, even to send guest information or direct mail. Use approved devices, access rights and network controls. Managers should clarify who uses information, for what purpose and how it is handled after work ends. Report suspected external transmission or loss promptly rather than handling it alone, and prevent further harm.

Material expelled by vomiting
Infection spreading from a source to another person

example.situation: During a busy check-in period, a colleague reports abdominal pain and diarrhea, while vomit is found in a corridor.
steps: Adjust the ill employee’s work.
Keep people away from the vomit and call trained staff.
Confirm protective equipment and current procedures and avoid unsafe lone handling.

practice.prompt: As a manager, identify the self-directed decisions to prohibit and the person to consult for training records, illness reports, vomit handling and information removal.
expectedPoints: Do not decide fitness for work from temperature alone
Maintain distance and protective equipment
Use the fire plan applicable to the facility
Do not transfer guest information to personal devices without authorization

questions.prompt: An employee with diarrhea says they can work because their temperature is below 37.5°C. What is appropriate?
choices: Decide attendance solely by temperature
Report symptoms and decide according to tasks and facility procedures
Tell them to conceal it because work is busy
Food handling is always safe
questions.explanation: Do not decide from a single temperature value. Report symptoms and work circumstances to the responsible person.

questions.prompt: What is appropriate immediately after finding vomit?
choices: Pick it up quickly with bare hands
Keep people away and contact trained staff
Vacuum it up
Mix several chemicals and spread them
questions.explanation: Protect the surrounding area and involve staff using suitable protection and procedures.

questions.prompt: Customer direct-mail work is unfinished. What is appropriate?
choices: Copy the entire register to a personal computer and take it home
Send the register to a friend for help
Consult the responsible person about work within approved systems and access rights
Transfer it to a USB drive without authorization
questions.explanation: A work purpose does not justify unauthorized removal of information.

questions.prompt: A linen cart is directly in front of a fire door. What is appropriate?
choices: Remove the obstruction according to procedures so the door can function
It is always acceptable for a short period
Add carts to hold the door in place
It is fine if guests do not see it
questions.explanation: Maintain fire-door function and unobstructed escape routes.

lessons.title: Manage food and bathing-facility hygiene
lessons.reading: しょくひんとよくじょうのえいせいをかんりする

objectives.text: Explain HACCP planning, action, records and review
Distinguish bacterial and viral prevention principles
Check the conditions for refrigeration, thawing and bath disinfection

sections.title: Connect plans to actual work and records
sections.body: In food-handling operations, identify hazards through HACCP-based management, establish a hygiene plan and communicate necessary procedures to employees. Record checks such as temperatures and cleaning and review whether the plan and procedures work. Following public health center guidance, managers should check that staff understand what to do, when, against which standard and how to respond to abnormalities. Never invent measurement values simply to fill in records. When processes or equipment change, check whether plans need revision.

sections.title: Manage refrigeration and thawing by food and facility conditions
sections.body: Do not merely look at a refrigerator display: check temperature using the method in the facility plan and report abnormalities. The textbook mentions 2–5°C, but do not treat this as a nationwide universal standard that overrides each food’s storage requirements and process conditions. If a reading is outside the applicable limit, consult the responsible person about causes and handling of the food. Thaw frozen food by an approved method suitable for the food and task rather than leaving it at room temperature for long periods. Cooling does not necessarily make contaminated food safe again.

sections.title: Do not describe bacteria and viruses identically
sections.body: For bacterial food poisoning, consider preventing contamination, limiting multiplication and reducing the organisms through appropriate treatment. Viruses do not multiply in food, so “prevent multiplication” does not apply in the same sense. For viruses, prevent introduction, prevent spread and food contamination, and use necessary heating or other appropriate controls. Learn norovirus, Salmonella and enterohemorrhagic E. coli O157 as examples, but do not limit each cause to one food. Do not identify the cause solely from symptoms or food appearance; pass information to the responsible person and public health center as appropriate.

sections.title: Do not judge bath disinfection by appearance alone
sections.body: Clear-looking water does not remove the need for hygiene management in recirculating baths. Staff must continue cleaning, disinfection, water-quality checks and records appropriate to facility conditions. Even with chlorine-based agents, water characteristics, pH, equipment and materials affect the method and effectiveness. Managers should check public health guidance, local ordinances and current management guidance, and ensure staff understand measurement and abnormality responses. “Add chlorine periodically” is not a complete operational procedure. Do not change chemical quantities or concentrations based only on experience; follow approved instructions.

sections.title: Manage equipment for broad usability
sections.body: Universal design at Level 2 is not limited to supplying a separate tool for a particular person. It aims for facilities and products usable by many people regardless of age, sex or disability. When someone reports a difficulty, confirm their usage situation and facility constraints and refer the issue to the improvement team. After changes, review guidance, cleaning and maintenance as well. Check actual use rather than judging only safety, hygiene or usability in isolation.

example.situation: The facility installs a new refrigerator and bath-disinfection system.
steps: Check approved management conditions for each food and item of equipment.
Explain measurement, records and reporting of abnormalities to staff.
Review subsequent records and conditions and revise the plan if needed.

practice.prompt: Correct these statements with reasons and conditions: “Refrigeration stops viruses multiplying in food”; “Every food is safe at 2–5°C”; “Adding chlorine completes hot-spring management.”
expectedPoints: Viruses do not multiply in food
Food-specific storage conditions and contamination prevention
Baths also require measurement, records and cleaning appropriate to conditions

questions.prompt: Which action follows HACCP-based hygiene management?
choices: Keep no records if there is no problem
Record guessed temperatures without measuring
Share the plan, implement it, record and verify results, and revise when necessary
Do not check procedures after equipment changes
questions.explanation: Hygiene management links planning to implementation, records and verification of effectiveness.

questions.prompt: Which statement about viral food poisoning is appropriate?
choices: Viruses multiply in food, so refrigeration alone completes prevention
Prevent introduction, spread and attachment to food, and carry out necessary treatment
Contamination is always visible
Viruses multiply exactly like bacteria
questions.explanation: Viruses do not multiply in food. Preventing introduction and spread of contamination is important.

questions.prompt: Which refrigeration practice is appropriate?
choices: Use one temperature for every food
Refrigeration always makes contaminated food safe
Watch the display without reporting abnormalities
Check food- and process-specific limits, measure and respond to abnormalities
questions.explanation: Do not treat one textbook number as a universal standard; use a plan appropriate to the food and process.

questions.prompt: Which management of a recirculating bath is appropriate?
choices: Continue cleaning, disinfection, measurement and records appropriate to conditions
Do not test if the water looks clear
Add chemicals by experience alone
No management is needed after one disinfection
questions.explanation: Observe water and equipment conditions and follow public health guidance and facility procedures.

questions.prompt: Which idea reflects universal design?
choices: Design only for a particular age group
Aim for usability by many people regardless of age or disability
Prioritize only low cost
Do not ask about users’ difficulties
questions.explanation: Aim for facilities and products that more people can use, without restricting the users assumed.
